<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a3ea67c2c02adbced1c43eda0f252eac3568123` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c53622d4fee261fdc86640ab3ddaf13899a641a0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md + packages/qa/scenarios/test/verified-builds.test.ts, docs/qa/scenarios/README.md, docs/qa/scenarios/builds/order_to_cash.provenance.json, docs/qa/scenarios/builds/travel_expense.provenance.json
Rule-change-verified: none

Read: card #34920 (body and all 11 comments), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main`, and the 74 check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The sha256 figures below are hashes of the head's own blobs (`git show`), which is a read of the tree. The 5,341-line build was read for shape only (top-level keys, manifest, a scan for paths and credentials: none).

The remainder of the diff (`docs/qa/scenarios/builds/order_to_cash.json`, `turbo.json`, `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `docs/qa/scenarios/builds/`: right.** The new test admits a build only with a provenance beside it that names the build and the card, a `sha256` equal to the file's, a `cardSha256` equal to the card in the tree, well-formed `amended` entries, and a protocol range the handshake reads as `ok`. On this head all hold:
  - `order_to_cash.json` hashes to `5d1696c8…fcea`, 152,377 bytes, as its provenance says; its card hashes to `fb53e5cf…7e02`, also at the runner sha `b620c4b2`, which is on `main` and is this PR's merge base.
  - `travel_expense.json` hashes to `cc035a91…709d` (unchanged); its card hashes to `a6ae8aa6…5ac9`, the re-pinned value.
  - Both manifests declare `engines.protocol` `^19`; `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `19.0.0`.
- **Dataset cards: right.** Exactly two cards carry `datasetQuestions` (`order_to_cash`, `travel_expense`), and `builds/` holds exactly those two.
- **Public surface: none changes.** `pack-library.mjs` copies `docs/qa/scenarios/*.json` one level deep, the loader reads the directory non-recursively, and `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. `builds/` and `test/` are not shipped.
- **Gate verdicts.** Test Core (10 shards and the roll-up), the Type Check family, the Lint families (the filter-parity self-test whose count moved 23 to 24 runs among them), Check Changeset, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard all concluded `success`. No check-run failed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — agreed. No changeset with `skip-changeset` matches what the diff publishes, which is nothing: no file under the package's `files[]` changes, and `builds/` is outside what the packed library copies. The claim listed a changeset; dropping it is the correct reading of the tree, and Check Changeset passed on the label.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1, no changeset:** accepted, see ②.
- **Deviation 2, three files outside the claim** (`turbo.json`, `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs`): accepted as a consequence of the claimed pin test. A test that reads `builds/*.json` needs the glob declared or a build edit does not re-run the suite. None of the three is a governed surface. They are the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- **`open_questions`:** none raised.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable. The diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- **Rule change.** The two changed hunks in the skill are a status note replaced by a check step, and a narrowing of wording. Neither alters what an agent may do without the maintainer, what a round does or in what order, or what must go to him. The set of cards an ask round runs is still §1's rule (the cards carrying `datasetQuestions`), unchanged. Verified `none`. The PR body carries no `Rule-change:` line yet; it needs `Rule-change: none` for the queue guard to have something to compare. That is a body edit and does not move the head.
- **Over the human-merge line.** 5,508 changed lines: Tier H whatever this record says.
- **Not measured at this head, for the seat:**
  - The card's Done-when names both dataset cards. The PR ran the ask round on `order_to_cash` only; `travel_expense` rests on #35222 and two later amendments. The new test pins its protocol range, not that it still installs.
  - The amended entry records `travel_expense` at Build 140/141 on the current scorer (`master-detail-inline-edit`). Ask rounds do not score Build, so no ask reading moves, but the fixture no longer passes Build at the current runner and nothing tracks that yet. It needs a card.
  - Both fixtures pin `^19`. The skill's ask-round example passes `--create-version VERSION`; a round that names an 18.x release there is refused at install. The PR's own ask round ran `--packages workspace`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`.claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md`** (two lines)

- §4 comment. The removed text ("order_to_cash's build waits on #34986, only travel_expense can run") is false on this tree: #34986 is closed and the build is in this diff. The replacement has the reader list `docs/qa/scenarios/builds/` before each card instead of recalling, the same shape as §1's rule for the card list. It holds against the tree: the path exists, and the runner's `templateProvenanceWarning` is the second line of defence when a build is stale. Holds.
- §5 sentence. "The verified build `--template` installs" replaces "the build a round installs". Against `src/runner/cli.ts`: an ask round without `--template` runs on that run's own scratch build, which is a run product, so the old wording did claim too much and the new one is correct for ask rounds. It closes the earlier review's note on this sentence. See N1 for the remaining breadth.
- Against the card's scope line ("records, recordings and logs stay out of the tree; a verified build that rounds run on is a fixture and is in it"): the sentence still says exactly that.

**`packages/qa/scenarios/test/verified-builds.test.ts`** against the README section and the skill

- "pins both sha256s": yes, both are recomputed from the files, not read from a second copy.
- "a build for every dataset card": yes, and the dataset cards come from the loader (`run.datasetQuestions`), the same set §1's `grep` reads.
- "a protocol range that admits the tree's own": yes, through `checkProtocolCompat`, the handshake the install uses. A build with no range reads `no-range` and fails, which is stricter than the sentence and safe.
- The failure messages state the README's remedies correctly (an `amended` entry for a hand edit; re-score and re-pin for a card edit; a new build when the reading changes).

**`docs/qa/scenarios/README.md`**

- The absolute-path sentence holds: `readFileSync(args.template)` at `src/runner/cli.ts:628` resolves against the package directory `pnpm --filter` runs in.
- The card-edit re-pin rule matches what the `travel_expense` provenance does in this diff and what the test's message prescribes.

**The two provenance files**

- `order_to_cash.provenance.json`: every field the README lists is present, plus the served model id beside the alias. Its figures match the tree where the tree can answer (both sha256s, the runner sha).
- `travel_expense.provenance.json`: the claim that the `masterDetail` mark does not reach the scorer holds in the code. `records-forms.master-detail-inline-edit` in `src/score/scenario-tags.ts` reads the build's own `master_detail` fields and field groups, never the card's mark; the mark is read by `prompts.ts` and `loader.ts` only. #37781 changed one line of the card. So the re-pin without a new build is right.

Tried to break it: a build edited without its provenance, a card edited without a re-pin, a build with no provenance, a build whose card is gone, a dataset card with no build, and a stale protocol range are each refused by one of the test's cases. A wrong `runner`, `built` or score in a provenance is not checked by anything, and cannot be without a live run.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the test's dataset-card case asserts `builds` EQUALS the dataset cards, so it also refuses a build for a card with no dataset. Its title, the README sentence and the PR body state one direction only, and §5 of the skill now reads as if any verified build `--template` installs lives in `builds/`. A template-mode build for a control card (§1, "not routine") would fail a case whose name does not say why. No effect on any current fixture or round.
- N2 (nit) — the README says an `amended` entry names the sha256 it replaced (`from`) or the card sha256 it replaced (`cardFrom`). The test's amended case checks `on`, `card`, `what` and `why` only, and its `Provenance` type omits both keys, so an entry naming neither passes. All three entries in the tree carry one.

**VERDICT: PASS**

- **Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** 7216905999 at this head: PASS, `No must-fix, no should-fix.`, `Rule-change-verified: none`; nits N1 (the dataset-card test also refuses a build for a card with no dataset, stated one way only) and N2 (the test does not check that an `amended` entry names `from` or `cardFrom`) accepted as deviations: no current fixture is affected. The seat adopts it.

- **Done-when.** `order_to_cash`: an ask-only round on the committed file installs, seeds 619/619 and answers 11/12, operations 6/6. `travel_expense`: the same bytes were installed by the eval area's ask probe today (9/13, operations 6/6, datasets 5/5).
- **Deviations accepted.** `skip-changeset`: `builds/` and `test/` are outside the package's `files[]`, nothing published changes. `turbo.json`, `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` register the new test's inputs; none is governed.
- **Out of scope, filed.** `travel_expense`'s build now fails `master-detail-inline-edit` under today's scorer: #37917.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Rule-change: none`. `Fixes #34920` is right.
- **Governance.** `.claude/**` plus 5,508 changed lines (a 5,341-line build fixture): over the human-merge line, Tier H.

Tier: H. Landing: hand-off to the maintainer follows this record.
